item: routes whose worker thread cannot start answer 409 and log it, not an unhandled 500
summary: A manager or job whose worker thread cannot start (the process or the machine is out of threads) raises RuntimeError, and the routes that call it mapped nothing, or only ValueError or their own refusal class, so the pull queue, the default-model install (Ollama and vLLM), the model-download batches, the dump, OSM and search re-index resumes, the search re-index start and the Start collection button answered an unhandled 500, with the 500 handler's log line gone once a status replaces it. Now each answers 409 (the exception's words, or the code worker-not-started on the three search re-index routes), logs the refused start at WARNING, saves no model preference when the download did not begin, and the Ollama batch refuses one model and goes on (all refused = nothing_to_do). Found by a scan of every start/resume/enqueue call in src/api and src/api/diagnostics (72 call sites); the scan went from 18 sites with no handler to 7 (the keyword fold's three, two start-up threads and two helper threads joined in one call). 27 tests, 16 red on the unchanged routes; 65 mutants killed. Limit: a refused collection start leaves the kill switch cleared with no loop running.
